After simplifying the expression, we get $(75+117i)z+\frac{96+144i}{z} = (75+117i)(4(\cos \theta + i \sin \theta)) + \frac{96+144i}{4(\cos \theta + i \sin \theta)}$.

Expanding and simplifying further, we get $(75+117i)(4(\cos \theta + i \sin \theta)) + \frac{96+144i}{4(\cos \theta + i \sin \theta)} = 300\cos \theta - 468\sin \theta + i(468\cos \theta + 300\sin \theta) + \frac{24}{\cos \theta} + i\frac{36}{\cos \theta}$.

Combining like terms, we get $(75+117i)z+\frac{96+144i}{z} = (300\cos \theta - 468\sin \theta + \frac{24}{\cos \theta}) + i(468\cos \theta + 300\sin \theta + \frac{36}{\cos \theta})$.

The real part of the expression is $300\cos \theta - 468\sin \theta + \frac{24}{\cos \theta}$.

Using the trigonometric identity $\cos^2 \theta + \sin^2 \theta = 1$, we can rewrite the real part as $300\cos \theta - 468\sin \theta + \frac{24}{\cos \theta} = 300\cos \theta - 468\sin \theta + 24\sec \theta$.

The maximum value of the expression occurs when $\sin^2 \theta = 0$ and $\sec \theta = 3$, which gives us a maximum value of $24(3) + 720 = 936$.
